result.summary:
Read-only headroom analysis. Data: the 711-run local formal batch (gemma-4-12b, thinking off; 77 analysed tasks × 3 samples × arms A/C1/C2) and the 316 runs of the 2026-09-25 paid batch (extracted into my own scratch dir). No models were run, and heldout_v34 was not read.

Short answer: no mechanism that only looks at whether steps had grounds gets to +15 pp on DABstep.

1. Harvest (writing down an answer the agent already computed) is nearly used up. Its ceiling for arm A is about +7 to +13 pp. My hand check of the matches gives about +6.9 pp; 16 of the 25 matched runs are real. v3 already got +7.4 pp. What is left over C2 is at most about 10 runs (+4.3 pp) by the loose count, and probably 1–4 runs.
2. Relaunching a fresh attempt when nothing was delivered is worth +5 to +7 pp on A locally and +9.7 pp on paid gemma-26b. On top of v3 it adds only +1.5 pp. Adding "answer written only after the reminder" as a relaunch trigger brings it to +2.6/+3.0 pp.
3. So the best process-only combination reaches about 62% against A's 51.9%, roughly +10 pp. It costs +54 to +90% prompt tokens, and it only works when a turn cap is stated and the model stalls under it.
4. For qwen-27b with thinking (the model that does not stall) there is about 0 headroom: 1 undelivered run per arm, and all its remaining errors are wrong answers that had grounds for every step.
5. An oracle best-of-3 would reach +18 pp, but majority vote adds nothing on C2. Legitimate process signals cover only about 8% of wrong answers (A: 0/28).

A gain of ≥ +15 pp therefore needs a real correctness signal. In this project that has only ever come from executable acceptance tests that are part of the request (LCB CONFORM +19 pp), and DABstep has none. Scripts and outputs are in /tmp/claude-0/review_effect/headroom/.

findings.claim: (a) Harvest ceiling on the local batch: arm A is 51.9%. If every run that delivered nothing had written its last short computed output, A would reach 62.8%; if it had written any correct value that was visible, 65.4%. A hand check of the matches brings this down to about +6.9 pp, and v3 already realised +7.4 pp. The value is usually visible early: in A's undelivered runs where it is visible (T1), it first appears at turn ≤8 in 23 of 31.
findings.evidence: A has 83 undelivered runs; 72 have an answer whose appearance in text can be checked. The correct value appears in a short computed output or assistant text (T1) in 31 of them, anywhere in the text (T2) in 39, and in the last short computed output in 25. By first-appearance turn, T1 splits into ≤8: 23, 9–12: 4, 13–15: 4. I hand-read the 25 'last output' matches: 16 are real computed answers. The other 9 are false matches: the name sits inside a candidate table, a JSON dump or a list of all merchants, for tasks 18, 61, 65, 67, 69 and 72. Two of the 16 are right only because the official scorer is tolerant: task 35 (28630 vs 28629) and task 7 (89.9997 vs 90). Recall check: in 100% of correct runs where the answer can be checked in text (A 107/107, C1 108/108, C2 120/120), the correct value appears in a T1 output. For C1 (current zero-config, no v3), the undelivered runs have 24 at T1 and 15 at last output.
findings.implication: Harvesting is a real lever. For this model, v3 has already taken almost all of it; a better-timed or better-worded reminder cannot add much.

findings.claim: (a) Where v3 captured and where it did not. 82 C2 runs got the reminder. 25 wrote after it and were right; 38 wrote after it and were wrong; 19 never wrote. Only about 10 C2 runs remain with the correct value visible (3 undelivered, 7 wrong deliveries).
findings.evidence: The 25 captured runs: in 20 the correct value was visible at T1 before the reminder (by first appearance: ≤8 turns 16, 9–12 4, 13+ 2, never 3). The 38 wrong writes: 31 never had the correct value visible, 7 did (tasks 18 s1/s2, 45 s1, 61 s2/s3, 66 s1/s2). Most of those 7 are candidate tables or cases where the model chose a different candidate. By content, the 63 answers written after the reminder are 43 values (24 right), 12 'Not Applicable' (1 right) and 8 prose answers (0 right). C2 still has 18 undelivered runs, 3 of them with a visible value. As a predictor of what the model writes after the reminder, the last-output measure is roughly calibrated: it predicted 19 right, 22 actually were (58 checkable runs).
findings.implication: What is left to harvest over C2 is at most about 10 runs (+4.3 pp), probably 1–4 runs. The cost of v3 is 38 extra wrong deliveries, and C2's wrong answers rose from A's 28 to 76.

findings.claim: (b) Relaunching when nothing was delivered adds +5.2 pp (up to 2 attempts) or +6.9 pp (up to 3) to A, but only +1.5 pp on top of v3. The best process-only combination is v3 plus a relaunch when there is no file or the answer was written only after the reminder: 61.9% (2 attempts) or 62.3% (3 attempts). That is about +10 pp over A.
findings.evidence: Method: the other samples of the same arm and task stand in for the fresh attempt, averaged over all 6 orderings of the 3 samples. A goes 0.519 → 0.571 / 0.589 (extra requests per task 5.0 / 9.0; extra prompt tokens +65% / +122%). C1 goes 0.532 → 0.569 / 0.582. C2 goes 0.593 → 0.608 on no-file alone (+14% tokens), and to 0.619 / 0.623 when late writes also trigger a relaunch (+54% / +90% tokens). In that rule the first attempt without a flag is delivered, otherwise the earliest attempt that has a file; the value is never judged. A's gain comes from 13 tasks where some samples delivered and others did not (1, 3, 6, 11, 26, 30, 51, 53, 59, 61, 66, 16, 44). Tasks where every sample loops (7, 23, 50, 58, 62, 65, 69) get nothing from relaunch; there only harvesting helps. Undelivered runs are the expensive ones: A's average 368K prompt tokens and a median of 159 s, against 96K tokens and 56 s for runs that delivered.
findings.implication: Relaunch and harvest cover different tasks, so they add up, but together they only reach about +10 pp at +50–90% compute. Relaunch is legitimate power to redo: it is triggered by a process fact and never picks a value. The comparison to beat is A given more turns, which today's data cannot measure (unclear).

findings.claim: (b, paid batch) Relaunch headroom depends on the model. gemma-4-26b with thinking goes 61.0% → 70.8% (+9.7 pp). qwen3.8-27b with thinking shows +0.0 pp: it delivered nothing in only 1 run per arm.
findings.evidence: Arms A and C serve as the two attempts, both orders averaged; this is fair because C had no measurable effect there (p = 0.21 / 0.29). For g4, A first gives 50 → 55 (same as investigation/two_runs.json) and C first 44 → 54; 0.34 extra attempts and 5.0 extra requests per task. Harvest in paid g4: the earlier hand-checked taxonomy found 6 strong + 3 weak runs in A and 8 + 1 in C that had stated a scorer-accepted answer (investigation/failure_taxonomy.md). My looser measure finds T1 in A 17/25 and C 23/28, and the value in the last 3 turns of thinking in A 14 and C 20. qwen: 0 undelivered runs with a visible value. Its errors are all wrong answers: A 8, C 12.
findings.implication: Harvest and relaunch only help a model that runs out of turns under a stated cap. Real pi use has no cap by default, so on a model like qwen, or without a cap, their headroom is about 0.

findings.claim: (c) Best-of and consistency, for reference only: an oracle choosing among 3 attempts would allow +18 pp over A, but majority vote gains nothing on C2. There is room, but no legitimate signal to reach it.
findings.evidence: pass@3: A 63.6%, C1 61.0%, C2 70.1%. Pooled over all 9 runs: 57/77 = 74.0%. 20 tasks were never solved in 9 runs (10, 18, 19, 36, 43, 49, 52, 56, 60, 67, 68, 71, 72, 1273, 1305, 1464, 1681, 1753, 1871, 2697); 26 were always solved. Majority of 3 (falling back to the first delivered answer): A 61.0%, C1 59.7%, C2 59.7%. In C2, 64 of 77 tasks have ≥2 agreeing answers, but only 45 of those are correct. The reminder makes the agent write the same wrong value repeatedly, so agreement stops meaning much. An oracle relaunch on wrong-or-missing answers with up to 3 attempts: A +11.7 pp, C2 +10.8 pp (to 70.1%).
findings.implication: The last +8 pp above the ~62% process ceiling need knowledge of correctness. Voting is not a substitute here, and it conflicts with 'never picks an answer'.

findings.claim: (d) Almost no wrong answers carry a signal Vacant could legitimately see. Across all arms, 12 of 142 wrong deliveries (8%) trip any grounds or format signal: A 0/28, C1 2/38, C2 10/76. The same signals also flag 17 of 380 correct deliveries.
findings.evidence: Counts are wrong deliveries flagged vs correct deliveries flagged. Failed step ignored: 2/142 vs 6/380 (both C2 task 1273, 'Not Applicable' written after a failure). Swallowed exception in code: 1 vs 3. manual.md never opened: 0 vs 0 (every delivered run opened the manual). Value never seen in any tool output: 8/129 vs 9/335; 7 of the 8 are C2 prose answers written after the reminder (tasks 65–68). Format mismatch with the stated format: 1 vs 1 ('7.683440%'). Prose answers are not a usable signal: 20 wrong vs 18 correct, because the official scorer accepts prose containing a single-word answer. The strongest discriminators are Vacant's own actions, not grounds: 'sent back and not resolved' 23 vs 9 (precision 0.72) and 'written only after the reminder' 38 vs 25 (0.60), against a base rate of 0.27. The paid batch's hand-checked taxonomy agrees: 0 of 27 wrong answers were catchable by the five checks, 2–3 by new process checks (task 71 undefined term).
findings.implication: Checking grounds cannot move the roughly 27–33% of runs that deliver wrong answers. The remaining headroom sits in those answers and needs a check that can actually be executed.

findings.claim: Which mechanism can reach ≥ +10–15 pp. On DABstep under a turn cap with a model that stalls, harvest plus relaunch-on-process-flag reaches about +10 pp over A and no more. With no cap, or with a model that does not stall, process-only headroom is about 0. ≥ +15 pp has only ever been measured in this project where the request carries executable acceptance tests and Vacant can redo work against them.
findings.evidence: Local: A 51.9% → C2 59.3% (realised) → C2 + relaunch 61.9–62.3% (ceiling). The oracle is 70.1%. Past results (ops/eval/evidence_20260925/investigation/past_results.md): acceptance tests plus resampling (CONFORM) on LCB v2 gave +19.17 pp (p = 0.0003); R460R, five replications, gave +14.2 to +19.2 pp over OFF. The G experiment (no executable judge) found no gain.
findings.implication: To get a clearly bigger effect while staying zero-config, target tasks whose request contains checkable examples or tests, where 'claimed tested but never ran them, or they failed' is a real grounds failure. That check then drives redo or relaunch. DABstep factoid questions cannot show more than about +10 pp for this product, and most of that comes from the cap.

findings.claim: For the 1-hour comparison set: 46 of the 77 tasks carry no information (26 always right, 20 never right in 9 runs). Every A-vs-C difference lives in the other 31 mixed tasks, and all six big-gain tasks (1, 23, 35, 44, 62, 69) are among them.
findings.evidence: Per-task table (A / C1 / C2 over the 3 samples): 31 tasks are mixed, and 21 of those have ≥1 undelivered A run. Tasks 35 and 69 gain partly through scorer tolerance (28630 vs 28629; '1m-5m' vs '5m'). Locally: 31 tasks × 2 arms × 1 sample = 62 runs, about 1.1 h at about 55 runs per hour. On the API with gemma-26b: about $0.012 per run, so about $0.75, which fits the ≈$1.40 budget. qwen is about $0.008 per run, but it has no headroom for this mechanism.
findings.implication: The set is picked from outcomes v3 was designed on, so its effects will look inflated. Use it only to screen quickly and confirm on held-out tasks. One sample of it can detect about +15 pp overall at best: the v3 effect of +7.4 pp gave McNemar 11v7 / 12v3 / 8v4, significant in only 1 of 3 samples.

result.summary:
Past-gains archaeology, verified against the source files rather than taken from earlier summaries. Every measured gain in correct deliveries came from a check that Vacant or the harness ran itself on the deliverable (a pass/fail it executed, not a reading of the transcript and not a model's opinion). In all the big cases that check was combined with a second chance: a fresh resample (CONFORM), a choice among 5 candidates (EQ5), or pasting the failure text back into the same conversation (H arms / R530 GATE). Refusal adds zero correct deliveries by construction (a refused task counts as a failure); it only cuts wrong deliveries. The LLM reviewer plus revise design (G experiment) added nothing, in 2 clean runs plus E3.

Isolated contributions:
- Choosing by executable visible tests instead of majority vote, on the same 5 candidates: +3.5 to +8.3 pp (3 of 4 preregistered runs significant).
- Resampling alone with majority vote: helps only on hard banks (+12.5 pp on LCB v2, +0.8 pp on MBPP+).
- Executable check plus resample (CONFORM) vs a single shot: +4.6 to +19.2 pp at 1.3–1.7× calls.
- Loop vs resample, when both feed back executable failure text: +0.6 to +5.8 pp, 0/5 Holm; with qwen3-27b it was −3.2 pp.

So whether Vacant can redo by fresh resample or by sending back into the same session matters little, provided the signal is executable. What decides the gain is whether the signal is real.

The two closest precedents to "Vacant on top of an agent that already loops" are both favourable, but neither is a settled result:
- R530, an agent that can run its own visible tests (preregistered, never settled; my recount): the gate that pastes failures back gave 27/59 fully correct vs 20/59 for the agent alone (b/c 12/5, p=0.14). Fresh resample gave 22/58.
- The only zero-config gain, the local v3 result (+7.4 pp, p=0.021, thin), is the same ingredient class: a machine-checkable signal (the requested file is missing) acted on while the agent can still act.

My R530 trace analysis also shows that the current zero-config rules deliberately ignore the cheapest executable signal. The agent alone declared done with the pinned visible tests failing in 25/59 cells, and 0 of those 25 were correct. Only 2 of the 25 final messages contain a pass claim, which is what `test_claim` needs to fire, and `failed_step` skips test runners. A rule that uses only the record ("last own test run failed, or tests present but never run") flags 30 cells, 29 of them wrong.

Single most transferable ingredient: a check of the deliverable that Vacant executes itself (file existence first, then the tests that already exist or that the agent itself ran), with the failure text placed in the agent's next input while it can still act. Not transferable without changing product shape:
- choosing among K candidates, or gated resampling (needs Vacant to hold the invocation: `vacant do`/headless, or a background copy at 2–5× cost);
- refusal (conflicts with the rule that a failed check always lets the delivery through, and adds no correct deliveries anyway);
- the reviewer (no gain anyway).

findings.claim: Every past measured gain in correct deliveries shares one ingredient: a pass/fail that Vacant or the harness obtained by executing something against the deliverable. Designs without one did not beat their controls.

findings.claim: The current zero-config rules deliberately ignore the cheapest executable signal: the agent's own failing test run before it says done.
findings.evidence:
vacant_network/trace/evidence.py:
- `_test_claim` (lines 570–608) fires only if the final message matches CLAIMS (a pass claim).
- `_failed_steps` (lines 624–626) skips any command matching RUNNERS.

In R530 SOLO, 25/59 cells were declared done with the pinned visible tests failing, and 0 of those 25 were hidden-correct. Only 2/25 final messages match CLAIMS.

A trace-only rule (my crude regex classifier, r530_solo_lasttest3/5.py) of the form 'the agent's last own test run exited non-zero (with or without later edits), or the workspace has tests the agent never ran':
- flags 30/59 cells, 29 of them hidden-incorrect
- catches 29 of the 39 incorrect SOLO deliveries

'Never ran the tests': 10 cells, 0 correct.

Caveat: in 11 of the 25 failing cells the agent had written into tests_visible/, so its own tests are not the acceptance tests.
findings.implication: This is a zero-config, zero-model-call extension within the 'did each step have grounds' principle: 'said done after its own test failed / never ran the tests that are there'. Its precision must be replayed on real pi/Claude traces before shipping; the paid batch's 8 send-backs were all false positives.

findings.claim: In agent hosts on code tasks, failures are mostly 'not delivered' rather than 'delivered with failing tests'. That makes timing the other half of the transferable ingredient.
findings.evidence:
pbgate runs, non-preregistered, n=1 per cell, gemma-12b, LCB v2 × 10 tasks (runs/pbgate_lcb2_20260919, pbgate2_agents_lcb2_20260920, pbgate3_backend_lcb2_20260920 SUMMARY.txt):

result.summary:
Mechanism review, read-only. I parsed all 711 local formal_v3 runs turn by turn (scripts and data are in /tmp/claude-0/review_effect/mechanism/: parse.py, common.py, loops.py, runs_turns.json.xz, plus a copy of the DABstep scorer, identical in all 80 tasks) and cross-checked against the paid-batch records (design/nudge_sim, ledger_all.jsonl.xz) and past runs (R460, R534, pbgate2).

Main conclusion: on this setting (gemma-4-12b with thinking off, DABstep 77, 15-turn cap), v3 has already taken most of what a "deliver what the agent already has" mechanism can take. What remains after C2 is mostly runs that never computed the right value. For numeric answers, the correct value ever appeared in some step's output in only 0/13 capped-wrong, 0/5 missing and 1/12 uncapped-wrong C2 runs.

Evaluating the five candidates on the local data:
- (1) Remind early when a value-shaped output appears: net harmful. Its 4 potential gains are outweighed by up to 14 runs it could damage.
- (2) Relaunch on no deliverable: +5.2 pp over A at +47% more turns, but only +1.5 pp over C2 at +10% more turns. It also goes past the person's stated turn cap.
- (3) Format or test checks: format checks reach 1 to 6 runs. On pi, test checks almost never fire (R534: 0 times).
- (4) 'unsourced': it fired 4 times in 346 reviews, all on task 38. Wrong answers are almost always printed by some step, so it cannot reach them.
- (5) Moving where the cap bites: no gain.
- My own addition, a reminder triggered by repeated commands (loop), works without a stated cap. On capped DABstep it adds about 0 to 2.6 pp over v3. Its only real value is in uncapped use, which has not been measured.

Why the old +14 to +19 pp gains do not carry over: they compared against single-shot generation. A pi-style loop alone already gave +17.5 pp over single-shot, and the acceptance gate on top of that added only +5 pp (not significant, R460). The A arm here is already a loop agent.

A clearly larger A-vs-C difference is plausible only where the mechanism's trigger is frequent:
- Tasks where A often runs out of turns: C2 − A was +19.4 pp on the 24 such tasks. This is measured on the same data that picked the tasks, so it is optimistic.
- Tighter caps: the harvestable headroom estimate is 14.3% at cap 15 and 18.6% at cap 10.
- gemma-4-26b with thinking: at turn 13, 11/77 A runs and 17/77 C runs could be rescued (manual audit in the paid batch).

Recommendation: do not build another send-back rule for DABstep. The cheapest informative API test needs no new code: A vs v3.4 on gemma-4-26b with thinking on, on tasks where the paid batch's A arm ran out of turns, about 48 runs, about $0.9. Treat it as exploratory, because v3 was designed from those same records. Relaunch is the only new "redo" power backed by a real signal (the requested file is missing), but it needs the human to decide whether Vacant may exceed a stated budget.

findings.claim: On the local setting, the remaining headroom after v3 (C2) is mostly out of reach for any mechanism that only makes the agent deliver what it already has.
findings.evidence: Local formal_v3, excluding tasks 5 and 70; C2 has 137 right, 18 missing, 76 wrong. For numeric answers (27 tasks with at least 3 significant digits; matched by the official scorer with no fewer decimals), the correct value ever appeared in a step's output in: C2 capped-wrong 0/13, C2 missing 0/5, C2 uncapped-wrong 1/12. By contrast, C2's capped-right runs had it in 10/11. Ceilings: at least one of 3 A samples is right on 49/77 tasks; for C2 54/77; across all 9 runs 57/77. Majority vote over 3 delivered answers gives A 47/77 (61.0%) and C2 46/77 (59.7%), versus C2 single run 59.3%. A solves 28 tasks 0 of 3 times.
findings.implication: A clearly bigger effect (≥ +15 pp) on gemma-12b/DABstep would need the model to compute better, or a perfect choice among several attempts (which means picking an answer). Neither is available under the product principle. Further tuning of the send-back or reminder family should be expected to add ≤ ~3–5 pp in total, which is within noise at 77×3.

findings.claim: Candidate (1), a reminder when the last tool output already has a value of the requested form, would probably do net harm. It was effectively already tested and rejected at the design stage.
findings.evidence: Simulated on A trajectories (trigger = first short interpreter output, ≤3 lines and ≤200 chars, before any write). A missing-at-cap: 25/72 runs fire; the first such value is correct in 4, wrong in 9, not checkable in 12. A runs that ended right without hitting the cap: 53/116 fire before their own write, and in 14 of them the first value was WRONG and was corrected later. Because gemma tends to write and then stop, those 14 are at risk. In C2's missing runs the first value was correct 0/5 times. The design-stage detector 'tool_short_output' on the paid gemma-26b runs (ops/eval/evidence_20260926_local/design/nudge_sim/run_output.txt) had in-hand precision 0.25 and caught 6/32 runs.
findings.implication: Do not build it. Principle fit is fine (no value quoted, zero config), but it is the 'early reminder' already measured as harmful; expected change is about −3 to +2 runs.

findings.claim: My addition: a reminder triggered by a loop (same tool call, or same short output, 3 times) while the requested file is still missing. This is the only trigger that works without a stated cap. Its extra gain over v3 on capped DABstep is about zero.
findings.evidence: The detector fires in 53/72 A missing-at-cap runs but only 2/116 A right uncapped runs and 1/26 A wrong uncapped runs. Loop turns in A missing runs range 6–15, median about 10. Harm cases (correct value appears only after the loop) number 1 in A-right and 1 in C2-right. For numeric answers, C2's remaining looped failures are 'never correct' (4 missing, 9 wrong) or 'correct only after the loop' (1+1), so extra gain is about 0. Counting name and list answers (a loose match) it is at most 6 runs (+2.6 pp). research_12b found reminders did not break repetition in 4 looping runs.
findings.implication: Build it only as a product feature for uncapped interactive use, where v3 does nothing; that benefit is unmeasured (likely time and cost, not score). It cannot be shown on a capped benchmark. Size: budget.py +~40 lines (loop signal from Evidence.window steps); PI_EXTENSION turn_end needs a path that does not require BUDGET (~10 JS lines, one more hook call per turn); a render_nudge variant with no budget line; ~6 tests. Nothing is sent when there is no loop or the file exists; the wording passes KS-1.

findings.claim: Candidate (2), relaunching one fresh attempt when no deliverable exists, is worth much less than the reminder on this setting. It also necessarily exceeds a stated turn cap.
findings.evidence: Leave-one-out estimate from the same arm's other samples: A 120→132 expected (+5.2 pp) for +1139/2406 turns (+47%); C1 +8.5 runs (+41% turns); C2 137→140.5 (+1.5 pp, +10% turns); A with up to 2 relaunches +16 (+6.9 pp). The gain comes from tasks where A runs out of turns 1 or 2 times out of 3 (+6 and +4 runs); tasks where A runs out every time contribute 0. Paid-batch estimate for gemma-26b: 50→55 (report §十). Harbor's cap extension counts per pi process, so a relaunch gets a fresh 15 turns. piexp exp2 shows continuing the same session after the abort sends a 16th request.
findings.implication: How it would work: in pi, at session_shutdown re-run process.execPath with the same process.argv (this keeps Harbor's --extension, --session-dir and the model flags), clear VACANT_PI_PARENT/SELF, set a guard against repeated relaunch, and pipe stdout (~70 JS + ~80 py lines plus a Harbor gate; Harbor would then see two session files, so trajectory and usage accounting is unclear). Claude Code and Codex would need a synchronous nested `claude -p` / `codex exec` inside the Stop hook (600 s timeout); the parent's printed result would still describe attempt 1. Whether Stop fires on max-turns there is unclear. Headless only: in the TUI it would override the person's Esc. What the person sees is a delivery-note line: 'attempt 1 ended without X; Vacant ran attempt 2; N turns beyond the stated budget'. Principle: zero config ✓, picks no answer ✓ (only one deliverable exists), identical bytes when nothing is wrong ✓, but it breaks the stated budget, so the human must decide. In any evaluation it must be reported as an unequal budget (like CONFORM's +0.71 calls).

findings.claim: Candidate (3), checking the deliverable against the requested format or running the tests, reaches few runs here. On a looping agent, running tests rarely fires.
findings.evidence: (a) Prose written into the answer file under the reminder: 6 C2 runs (tasks 65, 66, 67, 68). All were written at turn 14, so the unused second reminder slot at 1 turn left could flag 'the request asks for ONLY the answer; the file has N words'. The correct items appear in only 1 of the 6 prose texts, so ≤1–2 runs recoverable. (b) Percentage asked, fraction written (0.731 vs 73.15, 0.899997 vs 90, 0.014 vs 1.43, 0.015 vs 1.54, 0.089079 vs 8.91): C2 6, C1 4, A 2 runs. All 14 percentage questions among the 79 formal tasks have expected values ≥1, but the rule would be fitted to these very tasks, and percentages below 1 are common in real use. (c) Run tests or examples: DABstep has none; test_claim fired 0 times. R534 (pi + gemma-12b on LCB): 'fail then redo' fired 0 times. Cross-agent gate (DECISION_20260920_PUBLIC_BENCH_GATE_CROSSAGENT): of 11 blocked cells, 8 had no delivery and 3 delivered code that failed the visible tests; all 19 delivered cells passed the hidden tests.
findings.implication: (a) is cheap and low-risk (~25 py lines in budget.missing_outputs plus a line in render_nudge; based on the request's own words 'write ONLY') but worth ≤ +0.9 pp. (b) is a borderline 'judging' call and must be validated only on held-out tasks. (c) Running the request's examples or the project's tests is the closest thing to past gains, but on pi the failures are mostly 'no delivery' (including length cutoffs), not 'failing delivery'.

findings.claim: Candidate (4), the 'unsourced' check, almost never fires and cannot be made useful on DABstep, because wrong answers do have grounds.
findings.evidence: Across all C1+C2 chains: 346 review events, 21+20 send-backs; kinds: missing_output 23, failed_step 20, unsourced 4. All 4 unsourced were task 38, value '60.091667' (rounding direction), and the resent answer was still wrong. Why it rarely fires, by design (evidence.py _values): the corpus includes every step output and the data read; about 300×300 pairwise sums and ratios count as 'derived'; rounding tolerance is generous; values written by the agent's own program are exempt ('not_typed'); non-numeric answers (43/77 tasks are names, lists, yes/no or small numbers) are never checked. A strict test ('the delivered value is printed by some step') shows wrong answers are printed: A 27/28, C1 37/38, C2 55/63 non-trivial. The unprinted C2 ones are mostly prose from the reminder. It also flags right answers: task 31 ('C. both ip_address and email_address' vs 'C'), 3 per arm.
findings.implication: Leave it alone. The dominant errors (fraud rate counted by transactions instead of amount, wrong field, wrong filter) are made by the agent's own code and are grounded. Only independent recomputation would see them, which the report's path B puts at 2–3× cost and which amounts to picking an answer.

findings.claim: Candidate (5), changing where the cap bites, has no available gain.
findings.evidence: Reminder writes: 59 happen one turn after the first reminder and 6 two turns after, so the timing already converts. 19 reminded runs never wrote. v3-3 ('only report the missing file on the last turn') never triggered. In the paid gemma-26b simulation, reminding earlier is worse: at turn 12 there are 26 rescuable and 10 'right later, at risk'; at turn 13, 28 and 7 (A+C, manual committed+leaning). 'Reserving' the last turn is not implementable: a blocked tool call still ends the turn and the cap still aborts. Asking once more after the abort sends a 16th request (piexp exp2), which the v3 decision already rejected.
findings.implication: Keep the v3 timing. Changing K is a way of overfitting to the benchmark, not a mechanism gain.

findings.claim: Past gains do not carry over because the A arm is already a loop agent. Past +14 to +19 pp was CONFORM (visible tests + resampling + refusal) versus SINGLE-SHOT.
findings.evidence: R460 (DECISION_20260911_R460_FABLE_AUDIT_HARNESS): a pi-style feedback loop reached 75.83% vs single-shot +17.5 pp (p=0.0008), but vs CONFORM only +5.0 pp [−4.4, +13.3], p=0.345. R534: real pi never went through the gate's 'fail then redo' path. In local C2, of 82 runs that got the reminder, 25 wrote a right answer, 18 wrote a computed-but-wrong value, 15 wrote a guess ('Not Applicable' or 'yes'), 6 wrote prose, and 19 wrote nothing.
findings.implication: 'Executable acceptance + resampling' on top of an agent that already loops should be expected to add ≤ ~5 pp. The large historical number was the loop versus single-shot, and that contrast is now inside arm A. Tell the human this directly; it is why 'we had gains before' does not predict gains here.

findings.claim: The clearly larger effects are in regimes or strata where the v3 trigger (budget nearly used up, answer computed but not written) is common, not in new mechanisms.
findings.evidence: Local: on the 24 tasks where A ran out of turns without an answer in ≥2/3 samples, A 4/72 (6%), C1 6/72, C2 18/72 (25%), +19.4 pp. On the 35 tasks with ≥1/3 such runs, +17.1 pp. On the 15 tasks with 3/3, +13.3 pp. The same data chose the tasks, so these are optimistic. Cap sensitivity from A trajectories: if cut at cap 10, A gets 108/231 right; 98 runs have not written by turn 10, and 43 of them already show the correct value by turn 9 (upper bound +18.6%), versus 33 (+14.3%) at cap 15; realized v3 at 15 was +7.4, about half. Paid-batch gemma-26b with thinking, reminder at turn 13, rescuable: A 11/77, C 17/77 (manual committed+leaning), 20/154 committed-only, 11/154 strict regex; qwen 0.
findings.implication: For a fast A-vs-C screen, choose tasks using only A-arm history (e.g. the paid batch's gemma-A runs out of turns, or the local A-cap tasks listed in the numbers field), and state the scope ('tasks where the agent runs out of budget'). The largest honest effect available is v3 on budget-limited, thinking models, not a new rule.

findings.claim: In a one-hour screen, each mechanism should report its own proximal counters, so a mechanism can be judged without a noisy A/C score difference.
findings.evidence: v3 on 12b: 82 runs reached the reminder condition. 63 wrote within 1 turn (77%); 25 of those were right (40%). The A-arm base rate of 'reaching the cap without an answer' is 79/231 (34%). Local throughput is about 55 runs/hour. Paid gemma-26b: A $0.0116/run on average (12.3 requests, 144K prompt tokens), runs that hit the cap $0.0181, qwen $0.0078. $1.40 buys about 75–120 gemma-26b runs.
findings.implication: Projected effect ≈ base rate × P(write | trigger) × P(right | write) − harm. The first two factors can be estimated from about 20–30 runs in an hour. Suggested API step (no new code): A vs v3.4 on gemma-4-26b with thinking, 15-turn cap, about 24 cap-prone tasks chosen from paid-batch A records, 1 sample per arm, about 48 runs ≈ $0.9. Label it exploratory (v3 was designed from those records) and do not touch the held-out tasks.

result.diagnosis:
Why the current effect is small:

1. **The control arm already loops.** Every large past gain was measured against a single draw: CONFORM r447 +19.17 pp, and R460R ×5 +14.2 to +19.2 pp. Against a pi-style loop, the same executable gate added only +5.0 pp [−4.4, +13.3], p=0.345 (decisions/DECISION_20260911_R460_FABLE_AUDIT_HARNESS.md:44, H-PI vs CONFORM). Arm A here is pi, which already loops. So "we had gains before" does not predict gains here.

2. **Past gains needed a pass/fail run on the deliverable, and DABstep has none.**
   - Every past gain came from executing visible tests against the deliverable. DABstep has no tests: 0 of 714 local formal_v3 runs even invoked a test runner (grep over agent/pi.txt).
   - Wrong DABstep answers have grounds for every step. The wrong value is printed by the agent's own code in A 27/28, C1 37/38 and C2 55/63 wrong deliveries.
   - All legitimate grounds or format signals together flag 12 of 142 wrong deliveries (A 0/28), and they also flag 17 of 380 right ones.
   - The five send-back kinds cannot see a wrong decision: wrong field, wrong filter, a rate by count instead of by amount.

3. **The one lever DABstep offers is already used up.** That lever is "the answer was computed but never written before the 15-turn cap" (A: 83 of 231 runs undelivered, 67 of them by the cap).
   - v3's reminder harvested it: +7.4 pp. The realistic ceiling is about +7 to +10 pp (hand-checked harvest +6.9 pp; best process-only combination ≈62% vs A 51.9%).
   - Left over v3: +1.5 pp from relaunching when no file exists (+14% tokens), or +3.0 pp at +90% tokens.
   - Above that sits the oracle best-of-3 (70.1%), which requires knowing the right answer. Majority vote does not reach it (C2 59.7%), and choosing among answers is excluded by the principle.

4. **The lever only exists under a stated cap with a model that stalls.** qwen-27b with thinking had 1 undelivered run per arm, so zero headroom. Ordinary pi use has no cap. v3's gain is a benchmark-setting effect, not "install it and your usual agent does better".

5. **Dilution and thin statistics.**
   - 46 of 77 tasks carry no information: 26 always right, 20 never right in 9 runs. The whole difference lives in 31 mixed tasks, mostly in 6 of them (1, 23, 35, 44, 62, 69). Tasks 35 and 69 gain partly through scorer tolerance.
   - Over all 77: p=0.021, but the sign test gives p=0.13, and dropping any 2 of the 6 tasks gives p≥0.05 (CONCLUSION_20260926_ZERO_CONFIG_V3_LOCAL.md:14–38).
   - On the 24 tasks where the agent often runs out of turns, cross-validated, v3 wins 15 pairs vs 2 (+22 pp for that subset).

**Bottom line.** Under the product as defined, DABstep cannot show a clearly bigger effect than now: about +10 pp over A at most with a stated cap and a stalling model, about 0 otherwise. Gains of +15 pp or more have only ever been measured where the request carries executable checks.

**Where the product's own check has signal.** The check "did it really run the tests, was an error ignored" has signal on tasks with runnable tests or examples in the workspace, where agents say done after their own last test run failed or without running the tests.
- Precedent R530 (cline-style agent, gemma-4-12b, not pi; preregistered but never settled): 25/59 SOLO cells were declared done with visible tests failing, and 0 of those were correct. Pasting the failure back gave 27/59 correct vs 20/59 (b12/c5, p=0.14). Descriptive only.
- For pi this may be rare: pbgate had 5/80 cells done with visible tests failing, and in R534 "fail then redo" fired 0 times. Unclear until measured.

**LOCAL "S36"** (gemma-4-12b, thinking off, pi 0.87.1, 15-turn cap; A vs C; 1 sample per arm; 72 runs):

It is the only candidate with a measured DABstep signal, it needs no new code, and it asks whether the reminder harvests on a second, thinking model. Label it exploratory: v3 was designed from these same paid records.

- It uses the paid ledger, so the $4.80 hard cap still binds. Do not touch :18900. Set STOP_AT=4.70.

- Take 24 seeded points out of the about 39 A runs that reached turn 14 with no answer file and a tool call at turn 13.

**Stage 2 — end-to-end S26-api, A vs $S/local/wheel_v34, 26 pairs / 52 runs:**
- Run PAIRS=2 while the held-out batch shares this 4-CPU machine (4.7 GB free disk). About 61 min.
- The first pair doubles as a smoke test (screen_api.sh is untested). Check that C's agent/vacant_home logged the budget reminder where expected.

- **API GO** only if all three hold: U_api18 net (C-only minus A-only) ≥3, K_api8 net loss ≤1, and zero right-then-wrong-after-send-back events.
- **Error rates:** false GO 0.07 at no effect; power 0.53 at +15 pp and 0.73 at +22 pp within U.
- **Net 1–2 is inconclusive.** The budget has no room for a second stage, so treat it as not GO for new local scheduling and report it.
- **An API GO is a screen result** for 26b with thinking. It says nothing about local 12b.
- **An API NO-GO does not rule out +15 pp.**

**Budget that would make this properly meaningful:**
- A two-stage API screen, adding a second sample of U_api18 for $0.56: $0.26 + $0.67 + $0.56 = $1.49 + $0.30 reserve ≈ $1.80, so about $0.40 more than is left.

result.risks:
**Overreading the screens.** Every screen task list comes from the 77 dev tasks v3 was designed on. A GO is a subset screen result. It must not be quoted as an effect (鐵律 5), and ❌ "Vacant 讓 agent 做得更好" stays forbidden. Report effect sizes as subset effects.

**Regression to the mean.** Comparing a new C against the historical A runs that chose the tasks gives false GOs (the null paid v2.1 C scores U 4 vs 0). Always run A fresh in the same batch.

**Transfer.** An API result (26b with thinking) does not carry over to local 12b without thinking, and the reverse holds too. Task lists chosen on one setup enrich poorly on the other (disagreement 0.17).

**Low power.**
- API stage 2 detects +15 pp in U only 53% of the time; a NO-GO does not rule out +10 pp.
- Local S36 one-stage power at +15 pp in U is 0.51.
- Tier 0 measures only the next action, not the final result.

**Cap-setting effect.** Candidates 1, 3 and 4 act only under a stated turn cap and with a model that stalls; their headroom on qwen with thinking is 0. Chasing a bigger DABstep number with them is optimising the benchmark's cap, not the product the human described. Their real harm is more wrong answers delivered (C2 wrong went 28 → 76; 38 of 63 reminder writes were wrong).

**Shared machine and the preregistered batch.**
- The second proxy on :18901 and the Harbor containers run on the same 4-CPU box (4.7 GB free disk) as the held-out batch. Use PAIRS=2 and pause if held-out infra_voids rise.
- Do not touch :18900 or heldout_v34.
- Do not start S36 until the held-out batch and its reruns finish.

**Budget.**
- $1.397 is left and no top-up is assumed. Single capped runs cost up to $0.0645.
- STOP_AT=4.70 keeps a margin under the $4.80 cap.
- screen_api.sh and the API copy of nudge_probe are untested: smoke the first pair and the first 6 calls.
- The paid proxy config holds the OpenRouter key; start it, never read it.

**Candidate 2.**
- There is a false-positive history: all 8 paid send-backs were wrong.
- Its evidence is R530, which used a cline-style agent, not pi. That preregistration is recorded as unsettled with contradictory status (R531 vs paper_synthesis.md:219). Descriptive only.
- For pi the trigger may be rare (pbgate 5/80; R534 fired 0 times).
- Tests that were already failing and tests the agent wrote itself can produce wrong send-backs.
- Replay and adversarial review must come before shipping, and the byte-identical-when-clean property must be re-verified.

**Candidate 3** needs a human decision about going past a stated budget, and its Harbor usage accounting is unclear.

**Confirmation.** The remaining 274 DABstep tasks are all hard, so a 12b confirmation there risks a floor effect.

**Rejected, with reasons.** Do not revisit these without new evidence:
- An early reminder when a value-shaped output appears: fires in 25/72 missing runs with the first value right in only 4, and puts 14 right runs at risk.
- A reminder triggered by repeated commands: about 0 over v3 when capped; research_12b saw reminders fail to break repetition in 4 looping runs; value only in unmeasured uncapped use.
- Tuning the 'unsourced' check: fired 4 times in 346 reviews, all on task 38.
- Moving the reminder turn: no gain, and it overfits.
- Majority vote or best-of: picks answers, and C2 majority gives 59.7%.
- An LLM reviewer: the G experiment found no gain (p=0.79/0.45; revise net −3.5 pp).

verdicts.item: Candidate 1: v3.4 turn-budget reminder, unchanged, measured where it fires
verdicts.problems:
What holds: the model gets no value and no answer from Vacant. The text is KS-1 clean. First requests were byte-identical in 237/237 triples. I checked that the reminder code in wheel_v34 (review.py, budget.py) matches repo HEAD byte for byte.

What fails:

1. **It only works inside a harness.** `budget.turn_check` returns `allow` ('no stated budget') unless the agent's system prompt states a turn cap (vacant_network/trace/budget.py docstring, 誠實邊界 2; DECISION_20260926_ZERO_CONFIG_V3 §四.1; CONCLUSION_20260926_ZERO_CONFIG_V3_LOCAL §五). Plain pi has no cap. So the user in the product principle, who installs it and opens their usual agent, gets nothing from it. Screening it again on 26b only asks whether the reminder harvests answers inside Harbor.

2. **It causes answers with no grounds to be delivered, and skips the product's own check on them.**
   - `render_nudge` says 'Write your current best answer to … now'. That asks for an answer whether or not any step computed one.
   - Local batch: 63 writes after the reminder, 25 right and 38 wrong. C2 wrong answers went from A's 9/9/10 to 24/26/26 (conclusion §二–三). The plan also counts 15 guesses ('Not Applicable'/'yes'); I did not verify that number.
   - These writes happen at turn 14. Harbor aborts inside its own turn-end handler at turn 15, so pi never enters Stop. v3-3 fired 0 times: no pre-delivery check ran after turn 14 (conclusion §三). v3.2 reruns the grounds check after the session, but only writes the result to the person.
   - So the files the reminder produced are the ones that never get a send-back before delivery. That contradicts CLAUDE.md 具體後果 2 ('在交給人之前改好') and 口徑 5 ('讓依賴有根據').
   - For a person, a plausible wrong answer is worse than a missing one. The benchmark scores the two the same.

3. **The plan's GO rules never count 'missing turned into wrong' as harm.**
verdicts.fix:
- If it is screened, add harm terms to every GO rule:
  - new wrong deliveries in U (C wrong minus A wrong) must not exceed the net right gained;
  - report how many post-reminder writes have a value that never appeared in an earlier tool output (the conclusion already computed this: 21/25).
- Every outward sentence must carry 'only under a stated turn cap; no effect in ordinary uncapped use'.
- A wording tied to grounds would be a new variant (v3.5) and needs Tier 0 first. For example: 'if an earlier step already computed the result, write that result now; if not, say it has not been computed'.

verdicts.item: Candidate 2: grounds check for 'last test run failed or never ran'
verdicts.problems:
This is the only candidate that directly follows CLAUDE.md 具體後果 2 ('說測過有沒有真的跑、錯誤有沒有被忽略'). The pass or fail comes from the agent's own step, and it is silent when the run is clean. As specified, though, it would annoy interactive users and cause harm.

1. **It would fire when the agent is asking a question, not only at 'done'.** It drops the CLAIMS gate, which today limits `_test_claim` to turns where the agent claims tests pass (evidence.py:572). The zero-config Stop runs at every agent turn end, and zerostop.stop does not detect a question to the human. Example: the agent writes 'the assertion expects 3 but we return 4 — which behaviour do you want?'. That has no fail/error word, so MENTIONS_FAILURE misses it, and Vacant sends it back instead of letting it reach the person.

2. **Normal output would be read as failure.** FAIL_OUT includes `\bError:`, `Exception:` and `No such file`, and `_test_claim` checks it before PASS_OUT (evidence.py:584). A pytest run that shows '12 passed' but logged 'Error:' in its output counts as failed. Today the CLAIMS gate keeps this rare; without the gate it becomes common.

3. **Tests that were already failing trigger it.** The baseline is 'the first run of the same command', and that does not exist when the agent runs the suite once at the end, which is the common case. A send-back saying 'Fix it and re-run' then pushes the agent to edit unrelated tests. It would change files the person never asked to change.

4. **The plan contradicts itself on values.** It says 'no value' but also 'first failing line'. An assertion line often carries the expected value. That is consistent with failed_step's existing 80-character quote, but it is not 'no value'.

5. **The evidence is from a different agent.** It comes from R530, a cline-style agent that pasted failures back in a harness, not zero-config pi. For pi the trigger may be rare (pbgate 5/80; R534 fired 0 times). 'Up to +10 pp' does not transfer.

verdicts.item: Candidate 3: relaunch once when a capped run ends with no deliverable
verdicts.problems:
1. **It spends the user's money beyond their explicit budget, without asking.** The person stated a turn cap. Vacant starts a whole extra session (about +5 requests; +65% prompt tokens over A with up to 2 attempts), and says so only afterwards in a note.

2. **It cannot tell a cap stop from a user stop.** v3.1 records that pi reports an abort the same way for 'the cap or Esc' (DECISION_20260926_ZERO_CONFIG_V3 §六).
   - In headless use, a CI timeout sends SIGTERM, which also reaches session_shutdown. Re-executing there creates a process that outlives the kill.
   - In the TUI, re-executing process.argv starts a new interactive session.

3. **It turns Vacant into the thing that generates, not a check on the user's agent run as usual.** For Claude and Codex it needs a nested headless run inside the Stop hook.

4. **It was already rejected, and it is still cap-only.** DECISION_20260926_ZERO_CONFIG_V3 §三 rejected it ('超過上限…子 pi 在同一個資料夾會把自己當成子 agent'). Over v3 it adds +1.5 pp.
verdicts.fix: Do not build it as default behaviour. If the human wants it, make it an explicit opt-in: it may exist as an optional add-on, as long as nothing requires it. It would fire only on pi's max-turns abort, identified positively; never on SIGINT, SIGTERM or Esc; and never in the TUI. Report its compute as unequal.

verdicts.item: Candidate 4: check the answer file's shape at the last-turn slot
verdicts.problems:
1. **It reads the file's content.** v3's own boundary is 'look only at whether the file exists, not at its content' (budget.py 誠實邊界 1). Judging prose against an answer is a step toward judging correctness.

2. **It messages the model when the file exists.** The v3 reminder only fires when the file is missing, so this breaks that invariant.

3. **Its trigger is DABstep's wording.** 'Write ONLY the answer' is the benchmark's own instruction. A real request such as 'write only the summary to notes.md' expects prose, so it would fire falsely.

4. **It was fitted to the dev set and gains almost nothing.** It was fitted on tasks 65–68, it acts only under a cap, and the ceiling is ≤+0.9 pp.
verdicts.fix: Drop it. At most, put a line about the file's shape into the note for the person, never into the model request.

verdicts.item: Fast suite (local S36, API S26-api, Tier 0)
verdicts.problems:
What holds:
- A is run fresh.
- Arm C installs only with the user's own commands: `harbor_vacant.PiWithVacant` does pipx install plus `vacant install`, with no Vacant environment variables (原則 3).
- Tier 0 injects the product's own `render_nudge` text as a user message, and that text is identical in wheel_v34.

What fails:
1. **By construction it only detects cap harvesting.** U24 and U_api18 are chosen as tasks where A ran out of the 15-turn cap without writing answer.txt. It cannot register candidate 2 (0/714 runs used a test runner) or anything that acts in uncapped use. It meets the human's request for 'a task set that gives an A-vs-C comparison within an hour' only for the v3 family, not for the product.
2. **The harm gates count only right-turned-wrong.** The K-stratum loss and the right-then-wrong-after-send-back check both miss missing-turned-wrong, which is the main harm here (C2 wrong 28 → 76).
3. **All tasks are the 77 dev tasks v3 was designed on.**
verdicts.fix:
- Name it a 'cap-reminder screen' in every record.
- Add the new-wrong-delivery and write-with-no-grounds counts to screen_decide.py.
- Put the first-request byte-identity check between A and C into the screen's gate.
- Do not call anything 'the one-hour suite' until there is also a code stratum whose tests sit in the workspace and use a standard runner.

verdicts.item: API pilot (Tier 0 on paid requests, then S26-api end to end)
verdicts.problems:
1. **Stage 2 would disturb the preregistered held-out batch, unevenly.**
   - At review time: 4 held-out containers running (h34-g12-off-A-*/C3-*), nproc=4, / at 89% with 4.3 GB free.
   - PAIRS=2 adds 4 more containers.
   - Vacant's hooks in the C arm run under wall-clock limits:
     - a scan over 8 s moves to the background, so 'what was written is unknown';
     - the Stop subprocess has 330 s and lets everything through on failure.
   - CPU contention can therefore change what Vacant does in the held-out C arm but not in A. 'Pause if infra_voids rise' will not see that, because a let-through on failure is not an infra_void. Filling the disk risks infra_voids too.

2. **The GO rule has no delivered-wrong clause.** Same gap as candidate 1.

3. **A GO would only buy more cap-harvest runs.** The plan's own diagnosis calls that a benchmark-setting effect, so compute would go into optimising the harness cap.

What checks out: :18900 is the local-only proxy with its own ledger ($S/local/ledger, from ps), so the paid-ledger proxy on :18901 does not double-write. In paid mode orproxy injects its own key, so run_one.sh setting sk-fake-gate for bases other than 18900 is harmless.
verdicts.fix:
- Stage 1 uses no containers and may run now.
- Hold Stage 2 until the held-out batch and its reruns finish (about 04:00 UTC).
- Add: 'C's new wrong deliveries in U_api18 ≤ its net right gain'.
- Record in advance that an API GO licenses no product claim. If it is a GO by harvest only, the next local slot goes to candidate 2's replay and code smoke, not to more v3 re-runs.

verdicts.problems:
What holds: the preregistration is analysed first and not touched, candidate 3 waits for the human, and candidate 2 gets its own track.

1. **Step 3 would put benchmark code into the product.** It proposes 'LiveCodeBench with check_solution.py treated as a test command'. If that means adding check_solution.py to RUNNERS in evidence.py, it is special-casing for the eval (against 原則 3 and 'only works inside a harness').

2. **Step 0's replay cannot find false positives.** 'formal_v3 C chains must fire 0' is guaranteed, because no run used a test runner. It measures nothing about false positives in interactive use.

3. **Step 5 overrides the human's literal instruction.** It rules out re-running, while the human said '現在那些重新跑一次'. The same-bytes reasoning is sound, but the call belongs to the human.
verdicts.fix:
- Fix the task images (make the checker exit non-zero on failure, or ship the tests as pytest) rather than teaching Vacant about check_solution.py.
- Replay candidate 2 on interactive pi and TUI traces that include test runs and question turns.
- Present 'do not re-run the full 77×3' to the human as a recommendation with its reason, not as a decision.

result.overall:
None of the four candidates both fits the product principle and can show a clear effect on the proposed fast suite.

- **Candidate 1 (v3.4 reminder):** it gives no value or answer to the model, passes KS-1, and requests stay byte-identical. But it works only when a turn cap is stated, which a normal pi user never has. It turns missing answers into wrong deliveries (38/63 writes after the reminder were wrong; C2 wrong 28 → 76). And the product's own pre-delivery check never runs on those files, because Harbor aborts at turn 15 before Stop.
- **Candidate 3 (relaunch):** it goes past the person's stated budget and cannot tell a cap stop from Esc or SIGTERM.
- **Candidate 4 (answer shape):** it reads file content and triggers on DABstep's own wording.
- **Candidate 2 (last test run):** it is the only one aligned with 具體後果 2. It needs these closed before build:
  - dropping the CLAIMS gate makes it fire on question turns in interactive use;

verdicts.item: Fast suite S36 (local, U24 + K12, one hour)
verdicts.problems:
What reproduces:
- U24 and K12 lists; cross-validated rates 15/58 vs 2/58.
- Exact enumeration: P(GO) 0.782 one-stage / 0.924 two-stage for v3-like; C1-like 0.112 / 0.154; +15 pp 0.509 / 0.708.
- False GO 0.020 assumes b = 0.06. Realistic nulls: A-vs-A cross-validated b = 0.0625 and C1 b ≈ 0.10, giving 0.02–0.05 one-stage and up to 0.07 two-stage.
- Makespan from sim.py: 58.3 min median, 61.6 p90.
- Random-36 check: 53% / 15% with net ≥3, which is close to the plan's 51% / 20%.
- Always running A fresh correctly handles regression to the mean. In-sample, C1 would reach P(GO) 0.28.

Problems:

(a) The known-positive P(GO) is uncertain. A Dirichlet posterior on the 15/2/41 counts gives a 90% interval of 0.38–0.96 one-stage and 0.53–0.99 two-stage. So the rule 'if v3.4 does not GO, the suite is untrustworthy' would wrongly condemn a good suite roughly 8–45% of the time. One binary calibration outcome cannot validate the suite.

(b) The harm gate is weak. 'K12 net loss ≤2' fails only 17% of the time at a true 10 pp harm and 49% at 20 pp. The main known harm of reminder variants, missing turned into wrong in U, is not gated at all.

(c) The rule's artifacts are not fixed yet.
- screen_decide.py does not implement the 'right-then-wrong' tripwire.
- analyze_local.py is untested on a subset.

(d) The suite is enriched only for tasks where the agent stalls at the cap. A variant that fixes wrong decisions cannot show a gain on U24 or K12. So it is a screen for the v3 mechanism, not the general one-hour A-vs-C set the human asked for. The W stratum was dropped (sim D3 with W9: 74 min).

(e) 'One hour' covers stage 1 only. Stage 2 runs in 17% (v3-like) to 40% (+10 pp) of cases, which makes it about 1 h 45 min.

(f) The tasks are dev tasks, so a GO is a subset replication.
verdicts.fix:
Fix the rule file before any run:
- Add a wrong-delivery gate, e.g. C's wrong deliveries in U ≤ A's + k, or reminder-write precision ≥0.3.
- Implement the tripwire.
- Test analyze_local on a 36-task subset of formal_v3.
- Read the calibration against its predictive distribution (expected net ≈5.4 per 24 pairs). Treat a NO-GO as 'underpowered', not 'untrustworthy'.
- Offer the human a W stratum (or U+W) version for variants that do not act through the cap.

Statistically, though, an API NO-GO has a 27–47% chance even when the effect in U is +22 pp, and 47% at +15 pp. It also says nothing about 12b without thinking. Tying the free local S36 calibration to that result withholds the only test of whether the fast suite works.

The other parts hold:

result.overall:
Most of the plan's arithmetic reproduces. What I recomputed:
- The formal counts, the U24/K12 lists and the cross-validated 15/58 vs 2/58.
- All screen P(GO) figures (exact enumeration), the 58-minute and 42/61-minute makespans, and the API cost of about $0.94 against $1.397 left.

Five problems need fixing before any money or compute is spent:

1. **Tier 0 cannot stop a null.** Its pool includes the 7–10 paid A runs that wrote the answer anyway at request 14 or 15. A reminder that only pulls those writes forward yields an expected D0 of about 7.5, above the threshold of 4. Restrict the pool to the 25 runs that ended without a file.

2. **The rule script disagrees with the plan.** screen_decide.py applies the local thresholds to the API suite (GO ≥4, K loss ≤2), while the plan says GO ≥3 and K loss ≤1. The right-then-wrong tripwire is not implemented.

3. **No gate covers the main harm.** Both screens gate only on net correct, so turning 'missing' into 'wrong' (38 of 63 local reminder writes) is invisible. The K harm gates catch a 10 pp harm only 17–25% of the time.

4. **The suite calibration is too uncertain to judge from one run.** The 90% interval for P(GO) is 0.38–0.96, so a single NO-GO cannot mark the suite untrustworthy. The suite also detects only cap-stall variants.

5. **Three citations are misread.**
   - R460 H-PI vs CONFORM measures feedback against resampling, both gated. It does not measure a gate over a loop.
   - The paid relaunch gain is +6.5 pp over A, not +9.7 pp.
   - Candidate 2's recall is 19/39 for the send-back rule, not 29/39.

Error-rate ranges:
- API false GO: 0.04–0.15, not a flat 0.07.
- Local false GO: 0.02–0.07 at zero effect, and 0.11–0.15 for a C1-like variant.
